routing_warnings.description: The 22-second draft and its extended preview duration concern the independently requested preview artifact, not the three-video pilot package.
The commitment to model the full video on the last reference changes creative direction rather than the pilot package's count, duration, or export structure.
The broadcast-ready quality condition belongs to final technical finish; the accompanying 72-hour delivery deadline is project-management information and should not become a Requirement value.
The distinction between live-action footage, avatars, static-image animation, and realistic AI-generated scenes primarily defines the visual-generation method.
The instruction to create testimonial material independently is more specifically about the testimonial-content Requirement.
The rejected script failed the required reference-derived messaging direction rather than the obligation for the freelancer to originate production inputs.
The complaint that the preview visibly looked AI-generated is a realism failure, not a failure of input-sourcing responsibility.
The instruction to include both products belongs primarily to the two-product presentation Requirement.
The client requires the current creative not to copy the winning reference; this changes the direction of an individual ad rather than establishing diversity among campaign creatives.

The client sets aside independent creativity for the current version and requests adaptation of the last reference; this changes the individual ad's concept direction, not the distinct-angle strategy across multiple ads.
Using the last reference as the model for the full video changes the creative concept direction rather than independently establishing visual realism.
Creating AI-refined pack shots for the second product concerns product presentation rather than the realism of the human video scenes.
The commitment to refine and incorporate the second-product image belongs to the product-presentation Requirement.
The client reports that the preview looks obviously AI-generated, which is a realism failure rather than evidence about lip-sync accuracy or facial performance.

The instruction to set independent creativity aside changes the broader creative direction to reference adaptation; it does not explicitly remove the requirement to create testimonial material independently from unavailable customer recordings.
The feedback primarily changes keyword specificity and reference-derived messaging; message 64 separately reports the hook-specific failure.
This message establishes conversion performance as the campaign priority rather than changing the viral-style Requirement.
The observation that the preview looks obviously AI-generated primarily concerns visual realism.
The reported quality failure concerns the hooks and generic viral material rather than final technical finish.
The preview failure concerns visibly AI-generated and unrealistic visuals rather than color grading or final delivery finish.
The statement that the preview is not appealing concerns creative engagement rather than final technical finish.
The complaint that the hook is too indirect is independently relevant to the Direct Opening Hook Requirement.
The instruction that the complete script must be in Hindi belongs independently to the Hindi Localization Requirement.
The decision to suspend independent creativity and adapt the latest reference primarily changes the overall Creative Concept Direction.
The optional diabetes theme and second-product use concern the Two-Product Presentation Requirement rather than general reference-aligned messaging.
The complaint that the preview looks obviously AI-generated is a failure of visual realism rather than of the preview approval workflow.
The instruction to set independent creativity aside and adapt the last reference changes the creative concept direction.
The instruction to include both products changes the product-presentation Requirement.
